The test image shows two bell peppers with large, sunken, dark black/brown necrotic lesions covering much of the fruit surface. The lesions show concentric ring patterns — very characteristic of a fungal fruit rot. Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (sunken dark circular lesions on fruit) or **Phytophthora_Blight**.

Let me view one Anthracnose reference image.

The Anthracnose reference shows a bell pepper with a circular, sunken lesion with concentric rings — exactly the same pattern as the test image, just at an earlier stage. The test image shows the advanced form where lesions have expanded and turned deeply black, but the morphology (sunken, circular, concentric-ringed fruit rot on bell pepper) is a clear match.
